title: Ivo and the Compass
premise: Theo Zhou, a railroad engineer who maps closed lines for a government that keeps erasing them, is conscripted to find a vanished survey team along the Vell River. Following the river upstream with a broken compass inherited from his missing father, he discovers the team found a drowned town and a sealed archive the state will kill to keep closed. Betrayed by his handler and hunted by the survey's true sponsors, Theo must choose between publishing the truth and protecting the friend who saved him. In the end he burns his own maps, sends the archive to strangers downstream, and finally stops moving.
about_author: August Blackwood is a former land surveyor who spent a decade mapping rivers no one wanted named. He now writes adventure fiction from a cabin at the edge of a decommissioned rail line.

chapters.title: The Man Who Kept Moving
chapters.summary: Theo Zhou, POV. Theo surveys a decommissioned rail spur at dawn, establishing his habit of never sleeping twice in the same town. He finds a fresh government notice ordering all maps of the Vell River surrendered. Emotional beat: restless unease — the sense that stillness is more dangerous than motion.

chapters.title: Gear Without Ghosts
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. A survey team's camp appears intact but abandoned: instruments laid out, meals half-eaten, no tracks leaving. Theo photographs everything, then finds his father's old compass stamped with the survey's serial number. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into obsession — the past has followed him.

chapters.title: Conscripted
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Government agent Maren Kessler arrives and reveals the team's leader was Theo's father's old partner; she conscripts Theo with a threat wrapped in an offer. Emotional beat: resentment and reluctant curiosity as Theo realizes refusing means losing the compass — and the answers inside it.

chapters.title: Downstream of Everything
chapters.summary: Theo and Maren travel the closed rail line by handcar. Theo reads the landscape like a ledger of erasures: flooded farms, rerouted bridges, towns unlisted for forty years. Emotional beat: grief surfacing — every closed line is a memory someone paid to forget.

chapters.title: The Last Station
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. They shelter at a derelict station where an old caretaker, Ivo Brandt, recognizes the compass and calls it by its maker's name. Ivo warns them the river 'doesn't like being followed.' Emotional beat: warmth against the cold — the first ally who asks nothing.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. Maren's chapters reveal her orders: recover the team's records, allow no witnesses upstream. She watches Theo sleep and debates her conscience. Emotional beat: divided loyalty — she begins lying in her reports to protect him.

chapters.title: The Drowned Bell
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Low water exposes the bell tower of a town officially never built. Theo dives and retrieves a ledger listing his father as the town's surveyor. Emotional beat: vertigo of inheritance — his father's name where it should never be.

chapters.title: Signals
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. They find the missing survey team — three survivors hiding in a rail tunnel, starving, led by engineer Petra Osei, who says the fourth member went upstream 'to open it.' Petra distrusts Maren on sight. Emotional beat: fragile alliance built on shared evidence.

chapters.title: The Compass Lies
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo discovers the compass doesn't point north but toward the archive — his father built it as a key. Petra reveals the team was sent not to survey but to verify the town could stay buried. Emotional beat: betrayal at the level of the state itself.

chapters.title: Maren's Report
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. Maren files a false report claiming the team is dead, buying time but crossing a line. Her handler's reply quotes Theo's father's file — he didn't vanish; he was erased. Emotional beat: horror and resolve; her loyalty transfers from institution to person.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. The four travel the river's gorge, pursued by a second government team. Ivo appears at a crossing with supplies and a warning: the archive's keeper is still alive. Emotional beat: acceleration — the chase strips away every safe retreat.

chapters.title: The Keeper of the Source
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. At the river's forbidden source they find an old woman — the archive's keeper, and his father's last correspondent. She shows him a room of documents proving the town was flooded deliberately, with his father's protest letter as its centerpiece. Emotional beat: inheritance completed — the truth is his now.

chapters.title: Petra's Price
chapters.summary: Petra, POV. Petra confesses she signed the verification report to save her team, and the fourth member went upstream to destroy the archive rather than let it be used. Emotional beat: shame and courage — truth costs everyone differently.

chapters.title: The Second Team Arrives
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. The hunters breach the source; the keeper is killed buying the others time to seal the archive chamber. Theo's compass, the physical key, is the only way back in. Emotional beat: rage and guilt — following the river has a body count.

chapters.title: Kessler's Choice
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. Maren confronts her handler, is disavowed, and defects with the proof of the cover-up's chain of command. She and Theo finally speak honestly. Emotional beat: loyalty redefined — not to truth or state, but to each other.

chapters.title: What Theo Burns
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo burns his own life's maps to mislead the hunters, erasing the one thing that made him valuable. Emotional beat: sacrifice of identity — he stops being the man who keeps moving by destroying the reason he moves.

chapters.title: The Archive Opens
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Using the compass, Theo reopens the chamber and copies the core documents. Petra and the survivors carry copies out along three separate routes so no single capture can end it. Emotional beat: quiet triumph — truth distributed is truth protected.

chapters.title: The Fourth Man
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. They find the fourth team member at the source's edge, dying, who reveals he was ordered to kill Theo's father decades ago — and couldn't. Emotional beat: devastating closure; the mystery of the father resolves into mercy, not villainy.

chapters.title: Flood Season
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. The state moves to dynamite the gorge and drown the source forever. The group has one night to get the copies downstream before the water rises. Emotional beat: ticking-clock desperation — the river that hid the truth will now bury it.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Climax: a raft run down the flooded gorge with hunters on the banks, Ivo sacrificing his station as a decoy. Maren takes a bullet shielding the documents; Theo must choose between saving her and the copies — he refuses the choice, and barely manages both. Emotional beat: everything risked at once.

chapters.title: Strangers Downstream
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The copies reach newspapers, families of the drowned town, and a junior archivist who won't let them die in a drawer. The state's version collapses quietly. Emotional beat: vindication without victory — the truth belongs to everyone now, including the dead.

chapters.title: Where Theo Stops
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo rebuilds the drowned town's station with Ivo, plants the compass on his father's restored grave marker, and stays. Maren, recovering, chooses to stay too. Emotional beat: resolution — the man who kept moving finally plants himself where the truth came from.
